audit_note: Manual metadata audit: 5 test questions × top-3 chunks × strategy A. Fields checked: document_id (source), page (section index), topic_category, source URL. Auditor: Hoàng Minh Huy (author — conflict of interest noted).

hits.note: All fields present and accurate. Source URL matches Wikipedia article. topic_category=model is correct.

questions.question: What are the challenges of Retrieval-Augmented Generation?

hits.note: All fields correct. topic_category=retrieval matches filter.
Strategy A (no filter) returns this. topic_category=model is correct for the LLM article. For strategy C (with filter=retrieval), this chunk would have been excluded.

questions.limitation: Strategy A does not apply filter; rank 3 from LLM article has topic_category=model. This demonstrates why filter (strategy C) is valuable for category-scoped questions.

summary.filter_compliance_for_filter_questions: q16: 3/3, q17 (strategy A): 2/3 (expected — strategy A has no filter), q18: 3/3
summary.key_finding: All 15 metadata records are complete and correct: document_id, page, source URL, and topic_category are accurate. The page field (section index) correctly identifies which Wikipedia section each chunk came from. The usefulness of topic_category for filtering is demonstrated in q17 (strategy C would exclude the off-category LLM chunk at rank 3) and q18 (all 3 results correctly scoped to language_processing).
summary.one_limitation: The source URL contains URL-encoded parentheses (e.g., %28, %29) for articles like 'BERT (language model)' — this is correct but requires awareness when using the source field for direct linking.
